title: Computer Use in Claude Code (Pro/Max plans, March 2026)
description: Claude Code users on Pro and Max plans can enable native computer use — Claude can open files, run dev tools, point, click, and navigate GUI elements to perform tasks on the user's screen. First-party Anthropic feature (not an MCP). Operates at OS level: controls Terminal, Finder, any native app. Distinct from Bash tool (terminal-only), Better Playwright MCP (web browser only), and Terminator MCP (Windows third-party). Launched March 23, 2026 as a research preview.
version_introduced: ~v2.1.83 (March 23, 2026 launch); v2.1.85 first named changelog entry (bug fix for switch_display on multi-monitor)
redundancy_status: NOVEL — fills genuine gap in desktop GUI automation (no existing first-party equivalent)
redundancy_comparison: Terminator MCP (2026-03-23, Windows-only third-party) and Better Playwright MCP (web browser only) are closest but fundamentally different in scope. This is first-party, OS-level, cross-application desktop control.

findings: Confirmed first-party Anthropic feature — announced on claude.com/blog
macOS ONLY at launch — no Linux support, Windows on near-term roadmap per secondary sources
Full desktop GUI control, not browser-only — controls any macOS application
Requires Claude desktop app to be running; research preview status
Distinct from Computer Use API (consumer-facing, zero setup vs. developer API with beta headers)

platform_blocker: PRIMARY DEVELOPMENT MACHINE (requiem) IS LINUX. macOS-only launch means this capability is completely unavailable on the current platform. No Linux timeline confirmed.

evaluation.reasoning: The capability is genuinely novel and officially Anthropic-first-party, but it is completely unavailable on the primary development platform (Linux/requiem). Integration complexity scores 0 because macOS-only = impossible to integrate. Capability expansion scores 70 (high potential when available, but 0 practical value now). Community validation is 100 (official Anthropic). Platform blocker is definitive, not speculative — no Linux support was announced and no timeline exists. Scoring 58.5 = NEEDS_RESEARCH, but the research is complete: the blocker is known and binary.
evaluation.action: DEFERRED TO FUTURE: Move to pipeline/future/. Re-evaluate when Linux support is announced. Trigger: GitHub release notes or Anthropic blog post mentioning Linux computer use. No registry update needed now.
